To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
overproduction of a Candida albicans gene encoding a subunit (CaCCt8p) of the Cct complex suppresses morphogenesis and Ras2Val19 phenotypes in C.albicans and S.cerevisiae.
a chaperonin gene of the pathogenic fungus Candida albicans is able to suppress morphogenesis and Ras2pVal 19 phenotypes in C albicans and in Saccharomycescerevisiae.
a chaperonin suppresses morphogenesis and Ras2pVal phenotypes in S. cerevisia and C. albicans.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of a chaperonin in regulating the Ras2p pathway, which is essential for the morphogenesis of S. cerevisae and C. albicans.
the identification and characterization of a novel component of the Ras2 signal transduction pathway in S. cerevisae and C. albicans.
the role of chaperonins in the control of morphogenesis and the regulation of the cell cycle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CaCct8 is a suppressor of the hyphal phenotype in both C. albicans as well as in S. cerevisia.
CaCCT8 encodes a component of the chaperonin CCT that is involved in morphogenesis in both C. albicans as well as in S. cerevisia.

the chaperonin activity of C. albicans is essential for the normal growth of this yeast, and that the overexpression of the chaperonins can block morphogenesis in S. cerevisae and in C. albicas, and can block the morphogenesis of C. albicas induced by serum or starvation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a subunit of a chaperonin (Cct complex) can suppress Ras phenotypes and filamentous growth.
the chaperonin CaCct8 suppresses Ras2p-mediated morphogenesis and other Ras2p phenotypes.
a chaperonin can suppress the morphogenetic and other phenotypes of a constitutively active Ras2p.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of a single gene can suppress multiple phenotypes in both S. cerevisia and C. albicans.
the chaperonin Cct complex is involved in the regulation of morphogenesis in S. cerevisae and C. albicans.
CaCct8 suppresses hyphal morphogenetic pathways in C. albican.
